title: multi record writes per-agent rows, run metrics and deltas against the baseline and the report renders them
goal: multi record --dir DIR [--out FILE] merges into FILE (default the benchmarks results file) rows of the scenario multi, case the scenario, arm concurrent or sequential with the knob values; per agent and in total: input, out, cache_read, cache_write, cost, wall_s and turns; per run: dup_facts (bench_repro's claim match across agents), claims and claim_conflicts from the sandbox coord store, land_stops, rebase_s, right (lookup answers scored as agent_bench scores them) plus eval_passed (the area's frozen questions on the sandbox bare's main); a row whose arm starts with delta holds, per metric, the concurrent run's value minus the sequential run's of the same scenario; bench_report.multi_tables(rows) renders the per-scenario tables and deltas that benchmarks.py report writes in a section of kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.md; a replay's rows reach only --out

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print("check failed:", e); sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail

import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
T = tempfile.mkdtemp()
B = os.path.join(T, "bin"); os.mkdir(B)
MARK = os.path.join(T, "claude-was-started")
open(os.path.join(B, "claude"), "w").write("#!/bin/sh\necho started >> " + MARK + "\nexit 1\n")
os.chmod(os.path.join(B, "claude"), 0o755)
ENV = dict(os.environ, PATH=B + os.pathsep + os.environ["PATH"])
def bench(*a, ok=(0,), timeout=1200):
    r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "_tools/benchmarks.py", *a], capture_output=True, text=True, env=ENV, timeout=timeout)
    assert r.returncode in ok, (a, r.returncode, r.stdout[-600:], r.stderr[-600:])
    return r

import csv, hashlib
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import bench_report
sha = lambda: hashlib.sha256(open("kb/_self/reports/benchmarks.csv", "rb").read()).hexdigest()
first = sha()
out = os.path.join(T, "rows.csv")
for seq in ([], ["--sequential"]):
    d = os.path.join(T, "m" + ("-seq" if seq else ""))
    bench("multi", "run", "mixed", "--replay", "--dir", d, *seq)
    bench("multi", "record", "--dir", d, "--out", out)
m = [r for r in csv.DictReader(open(out, encoding="utf-8")) if r["scenario"] == "multi"]
arms = {r["arm"] for r in m}
assert any(a.startswith("concurrent") for a in arms) and any(a.startswith("sequential") for a in arms), arms
assert any(a.startswith("delta") for a in arms), arms
need = {"input", "out", "cache_read", "cache_write", "cost", "wall_s", "turns", "dup_facts", "claims", "claim_conflicts",
        "land_stops", "rebase_s", "right", "eval_passed"}
assert need <= {r["metric"] for r in m}, sorted(need - {r["metric"] for r in m})
md = bench_report.multi_tables(m)
assert "| mixed" in md and "delta" in md, md[:600]
assert sha() == first, "a replay's rows reached the results file"
assert not os.path.exists(MARK), "a replay started claude"

notes: One record per run as bench_report's other sections: the generated tables, never hand-written numbers. The sprint is proven by a dry run: this story's check replays the mixed scenario at once and one at a time and records both into a temporary --out. Its second check, report --check, passes before the work by design: a guard that the new section keeps the report and README in step with the rows.
